title.value: Randomized Exploration for Reinforcement Learning with General Value Function Approximation
title.justification: The title of the paper is stated at the beginning and throughout the document.
title.quote: Randomized Exploration for Reinforcement Learning with General Value Function Approximation

analysis.description: This paper proposes a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm inspired by the randomized least squares value iteration (RLSVI) algorithm and the optimism principle. The algorithm aims to drive exploration by perturbing training data with i.i.d. scalar noises for optimistic value function estimation. The approach achieves a regret bound for linear and general function approximations and demonstrates its empirical performance on difficult exploration tasks.

type.justification: The paper focuses on proposing a novel reinforcement learning algorithm and proving its theoretical properties, such as regret bounds.
type.quote: We prove the theoretical guarantees of LSVI-PHE and through experiments also demonstrate that it performs competitively against previous algorithms.

name.quote: Similar algorithms have been shown to work empirically, including SUNRISE (Lee et al., 2020), NoisyNet (Fortunato et al., 2017) and bootstrapped DQN (Osband et al., 2016a). However, the theoretical analysis of perturbation-based exploration is still missing.

is_contributed.quote: The main exploration idea is the well-known “optimism in the face of uncertainty (OFU)” principle, which leads to numerous upper confidence bound (UCB)-type algorithms. Another recently rediscovered exploration idea is Thompson sampling (TS).
